feed.title: Programming Languages — Useful Sites
feed.subtitle: An annotated directory of links on software, AI, security and science. Every entry states what the resource does and where it parts ways with its neighbours.

entry.title: Awesome C++
entry.summary: A list organising C++ libraries and frameworks by topic. Unlike general search it is a maintained, categorised starting map.

entry.title: Awesome Elixir
entry.summary: A library list for the Elixir language and Erlang ecosystem. Unlike a Hex package search it is curated and grouped by topic.

entry.title: Awesome Ruby
entry.summary: A list gathering Ruby libraries and tools category by category. Unlike a RubyGems search it is curated, current and grouped.

entry.title: Awesome Rust
entry.summary: A list organising Rust libraries and applications by topic. Unlike a crates.io search it is a curated, categorised and maintained starting map.

entry.title: Awesome Scala
entry.summary: A topic-by-topic list of Scala libraries and tools. Unlike scattered search it shows functional and big-data libraries together.

entry.title: C#
entry.summary: Microsoft’s general-purpose language for the .NET platform.

entry.title: Clojure
entry.summary: A modern Lisp dialect on the JVM, focused on immutability.

entry.title: Dart
entry.summary: Google’s client-oriented language, the one beneath Flutter.

entry.title: Elixir
entry.summary: A functional language on the Erlang VM, strong in scalability.

entry.title: Go
entry.summary: Google’s simple, fast-compiling language strong in concurrency — its official site.

entry.title: Haskell
entry.summary: A purely functional, statically typed programming language with lazy evaluation.

entry.title: JMH
entry.summary: An OpenJDK tool for microbenchmarking on the JVM that accounts for JIT effects that distort measurement. Unlike timing by hand it correctly handles traps like warmup and dead-code elimination.

entry.title: Julia
entry.summary: A high-performance, open-source language for scientific computing.

entry.title: Kotlin
entry.summary: A cross-platform language on the JVM, the preferred language for Android.

entry.title: Lua
entry.summary: A lightweight, embeddable scripting language, common in games and embedded systems.

entry.title: OpenJDK
entry.summary: The open-source reference implementation of the Java platform — where the language and JVM are developed. Unlike vendor distributions the standard itself is defined here.

entry.title: Perl
entry.summary: A dynamic, mature language strong in text processing and system scripting.

entry.title: PHP
entry.summary: One of the most common server-side languages of the web — its official docs.

entry.title: R
entry.summary: A language and environment designed for statistics and data analysis.

entry.title: Ruby
entry.summary: A multi-paradigm language foregrounding readability and developer happiness.

entry.title: Rust by Example
entry.summary: The official resource giving each concept as a runnable, editable code example. Unlike the book it cuts the prose and leads with the example — for those who learn by trying.

entry.title: Rust Playground
entry.summary: The official space to compile and run Rust code in the browser with no install. Unlike a local setup it gives compiler output and ASM/MIR via a shareable link.

entry.title: Rustlings
entry.summary: An exercise set teaching Rust by fixing small, broken snippets. Unlike reading-based resources it has you read and fix compiler errors by hand.

entry.title: Scala
entry.summary: A language on the JVM uniting object-oriented and functional programming.

entry.title: Swift
entry.summary: Apple’s safe, fast-compiled language, developed primarily for iOS.

entry.title: The Async Book
entry.summary: The official book on async/await and the Future model in Rust. Unlike general concurrency material it explains Rust’s distinctive, decoupled runtime approach.

entry.title: The Cargo Book
entry.summary: The official guide to Cargo, Rust’s package manager and build tool. Unlike scattered blogs it gathers dependencies, workspaces and publishing in one authoritative place.

entry.title: The Rust Programming Language
entry.summary: The official book teaching Rust from scratch (“the book”). Unlike third-party tutorials it builds the ownership and borrowing model step by step, from the language team itself.

entry.title: The Rust Reference
entry.summary: The official reference defining the language’s grammar and semantics. Unlike the book it is not a tutorial but the authoritative answer to “exactly how does Rust behave”.

entry.title: The Rustonomicon
entry.summary: An advanced book on the rules of unsafe Rust. Unlike the main book it covers what to watch for when you step outside the borrow checker.

entry.title: Vavr
entry.summary: A library bringing persistent collections and functional control structures to Java. Unlike the standard collections it foregrounds immutability and types like Try/Either.

entry.title: CIS 194 Haskell
entry.summary: The University of Pennsylvania’s Haskell course, with lecture notes and assignments public. The difference from a book is the homework — and since Haskell is learned by writing rather than reading, that difference matters.

entry.title: Learn You a Haskell
entry.summary: The community-maintained online edition of the best-known Haskell introduction. Against the academic Haskell texts the difference is tone: it gets to monads through drawings and incremental examples rather than category theory.

entry.title: LearnByExample
entry.summary: Teaches Python, SQL and R through runnable examples, opening each concept with one small piece of code. Against documentation the order is reversed — working example first, explanation after — which also makes it a fast syntax refresher.

entry.title: RubyGems Guides
entry.summary: The official guide to how RubyGems works and how to publish your own gem. Against the API reference it also explains the decisions — version numbering, dependency resolution, publishing policy.

entry.title: cppreference
entry.summary: The de facto reference for the C and C++ standard library, marking which standard (C++11/17/20/23) each feature landed in — a distinction tutorial sites usually skip.

entry.title: JS Exercises
entry.summary: Runnable JavaScript exercises in the browser, for consolidating after reading.

entry.title: Eloquent JavaScript
entry.summary: A free online classic that builds programming thinking rather than teaching syntax, with exercises runnable inside the book itself.

entry.title: A Byte of Python
entry.summary: An introductory Python book — short, direct and translated into dozens of languages, written for people entirely new to programming.

entry.title: Apache Maven
entry.summary: A tool doing dependency management and builds for Java with a standard project layout. Unlike collecting jars by hand it resolves dependencies from a central repository and defines a lifecycle.
